Here is a technical paragraph:

Distributed inference systems shard transformer weights across accelerators. Tensor parallelism splits each weight matrix along one dimension and synchronizes partial activations after every projection, which trades bandwidth for latency. Pipeline parallelism instead assigns contiguous layer ranges to each device and passes activations along a ring, reducing communication volume but introducing bubbles when batch depth is shallow. Expert parallelism routes each token to the devices holding its selected experts, so all-to-all traffic dominates at high expert counts. Hybrid sharding combines all three: weights are replicated within a node, tensor-parallel within the node's accelerators, and expert-parallel across nodes, with collective scheduling hidden behind asynchronous copies. The scheduler's unit of decision is the microbatch, whose shape determines both the communication pattern and the kernel selection layer.
